attempts.label: DANDI:001347
attempts.paper_title: Conserved brain-wide emergence of emotional response from sensory experience in humans and mice
attempts.entry_title: Eyepuff affect under ketamine in humans and mice (Kauvar, Richman, Liu et al. 2025)
attempts.summary: Most of the paper's main findings held up in this data. Ketamine cut late but not early eye closure in humans and mice, lowered persistent activity along the coding dimension in humans and mice, and shortened the human intrinsic timescale. The brain-wide spectral factors and the network and region changes also reproduced. Human beta phase locking fell under ketamine, but by more than the paper reports. In mice, the late drop along the emotion-like dimension failed with the Methods window, though the code's different window gives it, and the claimed lack of change in fast activity failed. Verbal reports and licking could not be tested because the dataset lacks them.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Kauvar, Richman, Liu et al. (2025) on dandiset 001347, which holds the human eyepuff behaviour, the iEEG recordings of seven participants with spectrogram products aggregated across them, and the mouse eyepuff behaviour, and on dandiset 001326, which holds the mouse Neuropixels recordings. It tests the eye-closure effects of ketamine and other drugs, the behavioural inclusion of iEEG participants, the NMF factors and cluster tests of the iEEG spectrograms, the human and mouse coding dimensions, timescales and coupling, and the mouse emotion-like dimension.

outcomes.statement: In the non-iEEG human cohort, late eye closure normalised by early eye closure is lower during ketamine than during saline (0.71 against 0.43, 4 participants).
outcomes.source: Figure 1E; Table S3, Fig. 1E; Results, Precisely timed affective behavior in mice and humans, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: Late eye closure, normalized by early eye closure (0.1 to 0.2 s after airpuff onset), decreases during ketamine (n = 4 human participants
outcomes.notes: Trials 3 to 40, ratio of trial means (Open A a, Open B a) gives saline 0.706 (s.e.m. 0.084) and ketamine 0.426 (0.121), lower in 4 of 4 participants, paired t = 3.703, p = 0.0342, the values of Table S3. The three other readings of Open A and Open B give 0.703 to 0.705 and 0.424 to 0.426, p = 0.030 to 0.035.
deviations: The eye-closure traces are taken as deposited (already normalised to the open eye); the eye sizes behind them are not in the files, so the normalisation cannot be repeated.
Saline is the pre_trials_data series by the code's label (p50-condition-labels-link).

outcomes.statement: In the non-iEEG cohort, late (affective) eye closure alone is lower during ketamine than during saline (0.59 against 0.34).
outcomes.source: fig. S1C; Table S3, fig. S1 C

outcomes.notes: Late eye closure 0.591 (s.e.m. 0.066) on saline and 0.343 (0.103) on ketamine, paired t = 3.653, p = 0.0354, lower in 4 of 4; trials 2 to 40 give t = 3.813, p = 0.0317.

outcomes.statement: In the non-iEEG cohort, dissociation (CADSS) is higher with ketamine than with saline (9.75 against 0.50).

outcomes.statement: Participants described the eyepuffs as unpleasant under saline, and under ketamine the aversive quality was largely abolished while the puffs were still noticed; participants with the strongest ketamine effect on eye closure reported the greatest change in experience.
outcomes.source: Figure 1F; fig. S1F; Results, Precisely timed affective behavior in mice and humans, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: subjective reports of the aversive quality of the stimulus were largely abolished by ketamine without blocking awareness of the eyepuffs
outcomes.notes: The verbal reports are not in the dataset. The four sub-h files hold only the 40 saline and 40 ketamine eye-closure trials and their time axis, and no other asset of 0.250528.0702 holds text from the non-iEEG cohort; the code record holds none either.

outcomes.statement: In the iEEG cohort, ketamine reduces the late (affective) phase of the eyepuff eye closure while the early reflexive phase remains.
outcomes.source: Figure 2C; Results, Brain-wide activity screen during emergence of affect in human beings, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: behavior in the independent iEEG-implanted inpatient cohort displayed a multiphasic eyepuff response with a ketamine-elicited selective decrease in the affective phase of the response
outcomes.notes: Means over the 7 participants of each participant's median trace. Late eye closure 0.541 preinfusion, 0.306 ketamine, 0.518 postinfusion, lower on ketamine in 7 of 7 against both (paired t = 2.908, p = 0.027 and 3.447, p = 0.014). Early eye closure 0.877, 0.850, 0.875; ketamine against preinfusion paired t = 1.318, p = 0.236. With the windows shifted 0.05 s later (the code's plotting origin) late 0.523, 0.284, 0.503 and early p = 0.210.
deviations: The paper reports no test; the criterion's paired t-test of early eye closure is applied to the per-participant window means of the median traces.

outcomes.source: fig. S14G; Table S3, fig. S14 G; Results, Brain-wide activity screen during emergence of affect in human beings, paragraph 9

outcomes.source: fig. S12A to S12D; Table S3, fig. S12 C and D; Results, Brain-wide activity screen during emergence of affect in human beings, paragraph 3

The 10 min of the preinfusion file before its first puff stand in for the 25-min pre-ketamine baseline (fig. S15B legend), which does not fit in the 20-min files; preinfusion windows exclude the eyepuff assay as in the Methods' phase-locking paragraph. The whole file is a variant.

outcomes.statement: Non-negative matrix factorisation of trial-averaged, puff-triggered channel spectrograms yields six shared spectrotemporal factors, with explained variance 0.47 on held-out trials, from 458 channels of 7 participants.
outcomes.source: Figure 2F and 2G; figs. S17 and S18; Table S3, Fig. 2G; Methods, Factorization
outcomes.quote: Factoring the responses into six components (Fig. 2G) was found to be optimal, with an explained variance ... of 0.47 on held-out trials and diminishing returns with more components
outcomes.notes: 458 channels from 7 participants (SD168 86, SD172 97, SD181 58, SD185 43, SD186 47, SD211 44, SD245 83) in the 21 regions. Refitting NMF (3 positive, 3 negative components) on the mean of the preinfusion and postinfusion training halves reproduces the deposited factors to within 3e-13 and the deposited loadings exactly, so the dataset's per-channel file is the input the paper factored. Held-out explained variance with six components is 0.466 under the code's reading (training reconstruction against test data, decode_utils.nmf_k_determination with do_refit_W_for_test = False) and 0.535 with loadings refitted on the test data. The test curve gains 0.081 (2 to 4 components) and 0.056 (4 to 6), then 0.014 or less per step. Elbow at 6 by the largest fall in gain (both readings), at 8 by the largest distance from the chord over 2 to 28 components, and at 6 by the chord rule when the range ends at 16, 20 or 24 components. The criterion holds under the largest-fall rule, which is assumed. Per participant the test explained variance is 0.292 (SD186) to 0.654 (SD211). Both Open G readings give the code's numbering [0, 2, 4, 5, 1, 3]. 12 of the 28 fits stop at scikit-learn's default 200 iterations, as in the paper's code.
deviations: The fit starts from the dataset's per-channel train and test means (sub-H_ses-sgramPerChannel.nwb), not from the LFP; these were shown to equal the means of odd and even trials of the per-trial file (code split 1 and 0) for one channel per participant and session.
Held-out explained variance follows decode_utils.nmf_k_determination (lines 136 to 291), which compares the training reconstruction with the test data; the refit reading is shown as a variant.

Assumed elbow rule: the largest fall in the gain of test explained variance between successive steps. The paper and code give none (the code hard-codes k_elbow = 3); the chord-distance rule gives 8 over the full range of fig. S17A.

outcomes.statement: All participants with strong dissociation (CADSS above 10) show ketamine-induced oscillations below 10 Hz, and high-CADSS participants tend to have a larger fraction of channels with such oscillations.
outcomes.source: fig. S27E to S27I; Results, Brain-wide activity screen during emergence of affect in human beings, paragraph 9
outcomes.quote: all participants with strong dissociation (CADSS score >10) exhibited low-frequency (<10 Hz) oscillations induced by ketamine
outcomes.notes: Approximate test on the 20-min LFP files, CADSS from the code record (SD168 9, SD172 30, SD181 10, SD185 0, SD186 33, SD211 26, SD245 39). Main reading (baseline the preinfusion and postinfusion files, ketamine the second half of the infusion file, prominence 0.1): every high-CADSS participant has at least one channel with a ketamine-unique oscillation below 10 Hz, SD172 28 of 97, SD186 4 of 47, SD211 6 of 44, SD245 8 of 83 (CADSS > 10, 4 of 4) and SD181 33 of 58 (>= 10, 5 of 5). This holds in 50 of 54 variants under each threshold; the 4 exceptions use the combined baseline with the wider-peak overlap rule, and SD245 has none in each. All hits are at new frequencies; with 3 ketamine segments the rank-sum route cannot reach p < 0.001 (lowest 0.0022). The detection is not specific to ketamine: low-CADSS participants also have such channels (SD168 5 of 86, SD185 2 of 43), and the second half of the postinfusion file against the preinfusion file gives them in all 7 participants (60 channels, against 97 for the infusion file with the same baseline); only 2 of the 4 participants with CADSS > 10 have more on infusion than in that reference. Second part (not required), exact label permutation, channel fraction 0.240 high against 0.054 low under >= 10 (p 0.048 over 21 assignments), 0.170 against 0.214 under > 10 (p 0.629 over 35). Cohort (b) cannot be separated from (a).
deviations: Assumption, windows as figs15 (ketamine the second half of the infusion file, about 30 to 40 min after infusion start, the criterion's fallback window); baseline the preinfusion and postinfusion files combined (Methods, "pre- and post-infusion windows were combined"), the preinfusion file alone and its first half as variants. Sleep and ictal periods not excluded (no annotations).

Assumptions where the Methods give no value, each with variants where it could matter, FOOOF fixed aperiodic mode fitted on 1 to 40 Hz (fooof 1.1.1), find_peaks prominence 0.1 (0.05 and 0.2 run), width at half prominence, 80% overlap on the narrower peak (wider run), single-linkage clustering, cluster frequency the median centre, one height per segment.
The label permutation is enumerated exactly over all assignments in place of 10,000 shuffles.

outcomes.statement: In humans, eyepuff-evoked activity along the persistent (beta band power) dimension falls during ketamine (1.36 to 0.41) and partly recovers after infusion (0.72).

outcomes.quote: Across species we observed a decrease, caused by ketamine, in eyepuff-triggered persistence that recovered post infusion (Fig. 6, C and D)

findings.statement: The non-iEEG files (sub-h009, h011, h012, h013, ses-P50) call their two series pre_trials_data and post_trials_data and do not say which is the saline and which the ketamine visit; the visits were a blinded crossover, so the names are not a visit order either. Only the paper's code (analyze_airpuff_p50.py) reads pre as saline.

The CADSS dissociation scores of both human cohorts (Figs. 1, 2D, figs. S1D, S14G, S27) and the non-iEEG participants' verbal reports (Fig. 1F, fig. S1F) are not in the dataset; the scores are in the paper's code record (data/cadss_across_pts.csv and constants in analyze_airpuff_p50.py).

The iEEG behaviour and LFP files name sessions baseline, preinfusion, infusion, postinfusion, postinfusionfast and control without saying when each was recorded; the code's DATASETS.py says baseline is the day before infusion. For SD168, SD172, SD242 and SD245 the behaviour file holds a baseline session and no preinfusion session, and the paper treats that baseline as preinfusion.

The 142 head-fixed mouse behaviour files (sub-mouse/sub-mouse_ses-<id>_behavior.nwb) carry no label of drug, dose, mouse, sex, day, puff pressure or skipped puff; subject_id equals the session id, sex is "O" and age "P8W/" in every file, and the trials have no timestamps. The labels exist only as experiment-id lists in the paper's scripts (Zenodo 14920570, mouse_eyepuff/scripts/fig1_*.py), so no analysis can be run from the dataset alone, sessions of the same mouse cannot be paired from the data, and the Methods' rule for post-infusion trials (at least 3 min after injection) cannot be applied.

The Neuropixels-rig behaviour (eye closure) of 3 of the 13 recorded sessions of Fig. 4B (Table S3) is not in 001347: the 001326 sessions of 2023-02-25 (sub-3) and 2023-07-06 and 2023-08-22 (sub-5) have no sub-m* behaviour file; the paper's converter lists only the 10 deposited sessions (its commented "extra" list, printed in 02, names m95-544 of 2022-02-23, m11210-961, m11217-1104 and m11217-1107).
The lick data of the liquid-reward eyepuff assay (fig. S4, 6 mice) are not in the dataset or in 001326, and the code record has no script for them.

Table S3, fig. S2 C, gives saline affective eye closure on the first puff as 0.34 +/- 0.07, while the per-mouse values that reproduce its paired test exactly (t = 4.951) have mean 0.203 (s.e.m. 0.047).

Table S3, fig. S2 E, reports the Kaplan-Meier persistence of 15.16 s for 20 preinfusion trials per mouse (100 trials); fig1_persistence.py uses all 40 trials of each saline session (200 trials, pre and post injection), which gives 15.16 s exactly; the 100 preinfusion trials give 13.05 s from the code's start frame. The code's start frame is also 3.3 s after the eighth puff while the figure axis reads time from the final puff.

Table S3, fig. S6 F, calls the fast early (0-40 ms) comparison a paired t-test; fig1_muscimol.py runs independent t-tests (get_drug_comparison_pvals without do_paired), whose values (t = 0.37, p = 0.8898) are those reported.

Open I: the Methods count as post infusion only trials at least 3 min after the injection, the code uses trials 23 to 37, and the fig. S2B/S2C legends give 18 trials. The sub-mouse files hold no trial times. Which trials did the paper use, and how long after the injection did trial 21 start? (Here the code's trials are used, trials 23 to 40 as a variant; all conclusions agree.)

The Methods scale each mouse trial by 1/(1 - baseline), the baseline averaged over the first two trials; the code computes the baseline after subtracting each trial's own first 2 s, so the factor is one. Which was used for the absolute values of figs. S2B, S2C, S5D and S5E? (The code's reproduces Table S3's t values exactly; the Methods' changes fig. S2B's saline early value to 0.72.)

No recording is deposited twice among the 142 sub-mouse files (no identical file, first 20 trials or single 81-s trial; highest correlation between sessions 0.91, 1023 and 1026) or the 10 Neuropixels-rig files. Ids 282-286 are reused by the scripts for saline, female and the converter's sal_skip; ids 1020-1027 for ketamine 35 mg/kg and 28 PSI.

The per-participant LFP files are 20-min windows around each eyepuff session with no infusion start time, no epochs and no sleep or seizure annotations, so the 25-min pre-infusion baseline of fig. S15 and the phase-locking analysis is not in the dataset, and the peak-ketamine window of figs. S15 and S27 can be placed only from the Methods' "approximately 30 minutes after the infusion start" for the infusion eyepuff session. No CADSS scores are in the behaviour files.
Spontaneous blink onsets for fig. S12 are not in the dataset; they are a hand-made list in the code record (for_reference/analyze_airpuff_ieeg_natural_blinks.py lines 42 to 79).

For authors - how was the elbow of fig. S17A at six components chosen? The code hard-codes k_elbow = 3. On the dataset the test curve's largest fall in gain is at six components, but the point farthest from the chord over the plotted range (2 to 28 components) is at eight.

Table S3 (Fig. 2I) gives 5 participants for factor 3 and 6 for factor 4, but the deposited loadings, which reproduce every coefficient and channel count of Table S3, have kept channels from all 7 participants for every factor (factor 3 - SD168 19, SD172 28, SD181 22, SD185 23, SD186 13, SD211 19, SD245 34).

The deposited Fig. 2H matrix (yeo_loading_mtx_pre) does not fully match the Results text - factors 3 to 5 carry 0.495 of the limbic row and 0.463 of the frontoparietal row, while the text says these networks load heavily on factors 3 to 5.

The time bins of the per-network and per-region files (-0.531 to 1.444 s) are offset by 0.6 ms from the corresponding bins of the per-channel per-trial file (-0.532 to 1.443 s); immaterial for the analyses here.

The iEEG files do not mark bad channels, although the paper removes them; the list exists only in the paper's code (ketman/analyze/utils.py, bad_ch, 10 to 33 contacts per participant). With and without it the CD results differ in the second decimal and decide two readings of fig6e.

The electrode tables hold a region label per contact but no Yeo7 or Yeo17 network label, and x, y, z and impedance are NaN for every contact; the network labels used by figs. S19 to S25 and S35 are only in the code record (anat/pts_ch_labels.pkl).

The LFP ElectricalSeries (processing/ecephys/LFP/v_trace) declares unit 'volts' with conversion 1.0, but the values are digitiser units (1st to 99th percentiles of order 300 to 3000); the scale (0.390625 or 0.09765625 microvolts per unit) is only in the series comment and the device description.
The puff TTL is DC channel index 2, named 'CCEP' in four participants' files and 'DC03' in three (SD168, SD172, SD245); no description identifies it as the puff sync channel.

For SD245 the code's coding-dimension path loads both the Baseline and Preinfusion files and renames 'baseline' to 'preinfusion', so the Baseline file (day before) replaces the Preinfusion file, while the timescale path keeps the Preinfusion file. The behaviour file of SD245 holds only 'baseline' events. The paper's numbers for Fig. 6C and 6G are recovered only with this mixture (fig6g means with the Baseline file are outside tolerance).

Table S3 gives two statistics for the same postinfusion against ketamine test of the beta fast projection, t = 0.576, p = 0.585 (Fig. 6E) and t = 1.063, p = 0.657 (fig. S37B beta); the data give t = 1.072, BH p = 0.650, matching the fig. S37B row.

Question for the authors, Open C. Is the human projection z-scored over -1.0 to 1.5 s with the -1.0 to 0 s mean subtracted and summarised on a time axis shifted by 0.05 s (code), or over -0.5 to 1.5 s with the -0.5 to 0 s baseline (Methods)? The code's reading reproduces Table S3 to the third decimal; the Methods' reading gives a preinfusion persistent mean of about 1.63 and makes the low-gamma fast test significant.

Question for the authors, fig. S38H. Were the single-trial persistent projections baseline-subtracted over 0.5 to 0 s before each puff? The code comments this out, but the paper's coefficient (12.12) is recovered only with it (12.38 here; about 2.5 to 6 without).

Question for the authors, Fig. 6I and fig. S38. Which channels, windows (stride, exclusion of epileptic and sleep periods) and sessions enter the phase-locking analysis, and how were the 716 edges of fig. S38 selected? Selections here give 339 to 1020 edges and none gives 716, a ketamine ratio of 0.926 to 0.963 against 0.979, and, with the weights of each band, baseline differences between high and low edges in theta and alpha.

Question for the authors, fig. S37A. Which mouse sessions, mouse projection (first puff or all puffs of a series) and time range enter the cross-species correlation? Beta and broadband differ by less than 0.03 in r, and the order changes with these choices.
In all 13 NWB files of DANDI:001326 (0.250528.1957) the spike times of every unit (9554 of 9554) are stored out of order; they must be sorted before use.

DANDI:001326 numbers its subjects 0 to 9 and gives recording dates, with no link to the paper's mouse or experiment identifiers or to the Neuropixels-rig behaviour files of DANDI:001347 (sub-m<mouse>-<experiment>). Matching inter-series intervals links 10 of the 13 sessions to a behaviour file (all intervals equal within 0.02 s); sub-3 ses-20230225 and both sub-5 sessions have no behaviour file in DANDI:001347.

The Methods exclude one animal "that exhibited notable stress response" from the cross-puff and population analyses (11 sessions from 9 mice), but neither the paper, the code nor the dataset says which. Mouse 5 is the only exclusion that also gives the tone analysis its 7 sessions from 7 mice; with it the Fig. 6D statistics come out as in Table S3. Which animal was excluded?

The mouse code (Zenodo 14876694, analysis.py) differs from the Methods in several mouse analyses: coding-dimension weights are divided by a pooled scalar variance (compute_cd_cov), not per-neuron variances; the emotion-like dimension's target window is bins 400:500 of the post-series window, which the plotting offsets place 3 to 4 s after the last puff, not 5 s; the fast dimension's reference is the 70 ms before the puff, not the 1 s; coupling selects signed weights above the 90th percentile of |w| and takes the median |r| over concatenated windows; tone coupling uses windows before puff series. The pooled variance decides the mouse coupling result (Fig. 6J, fig. S34H) and the 3 to 4 s window the Fig. 5E test.

The Methods (Comparison of rates) define the Ketamine and Post epochs as trials 22 to 32 and 34 to 40 (11 and 7 trials), while Table S3 gives 10 and 6 trials for Figs. 5D, 5E, 6D and 6F, as the code's slices (23 to 32, 35 to 40) do. The recovery test of Fig. 6D is significant with the code's trials (corrected p = 0.029) and not with the Methods' (0.17).

The mouse code record holds no driver script: the z-scoring that makes all_zfr, the session filter (filter_session), the shifted windows used for the timescale (shift_psth_pre/post), the start of the post-series window used for the emotion-like dimension, and the dose conditions and trace processing of the Fig. 5H and 5I fits are not given. Which window (3 to 4 s or 5 to 6 s after the last puff) and which variance (per neuron or pooled) did the published Figs. 5E and 6J use?
sub-5 ses-20230706 has 2 Neuropixels probes and 154 units, where the Methods state 3 to 4 probes per session; it belongs to the mouse taken as excluded.

Question for the authors, Fig. 4B and 5B. Were the across-session eye-closure traces of the Neuropixels mice divided by each condition's maximum, as make_puffseries_behavior_plot in analysis.py (Zenodo 14876694) does, although Table S3 and fig1_npx_behavior.py do not? With that normalisation late eye closure separates between preinfusion and ketamine (0.630 against 0.318); without it the 95% intervals overlap (0.174 against 0.147).

Question for the authors, human coding dimension. Are white-matter contacts excluded from the coding dimension, as the code does (use_all_channels = False), while the Methods say so only for the phase-locking analysis? Both readings reproduce Fig. 6C, but with white matter kept the theta reduction and the delta recovery of fig. S37C lose significance and broadband becomes significant.

The fig. S38 legend classifies sites as high or low persistence "for CDs computed using power in each spectral band", while the fig. S38 code (for_reference/analyze_airpuff_ieeg_top_cd_network.py lines 231 to 232) says its version "uses beta CD weights 0.5-1.5 to sort top v bot CD electrodes". With the weights of each band preinfusion theta and alpha coupling differ between high and low edges in 38 of 44 readings; with beta weights for every band no band differs in 20 of 20.

entries.name: kauvar-2025-001326
entries.title: Brain-wide mouse electrophysiology during eyepuffs and ketamine (Kauvar, Richman, Liu et al. 2025)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Kauvar, Richman, Liu et al. (2025) on dandiset 001326, which holds Neuropixels recordings of 13 sessions from 10 mice during eyepuff and tone series before and after ketamine, and the behavior in dandiset 001347. The first notebook covers the response clusters and their regional distribution, regional rise and decay times, the emotion-like population dimension and its first-order model, the fast and persistent coding dimensions with their baseline timescale and coupling, the tone responses, and the resting correlation structure and spectra. The second covers the eye closure of the recorded mice, the behavior-only mouse drug, dose, pressure and muscimol experiments, and the eye closure of four non-implanted participants, from dandiset 001347. The third covers the human iEEG factor analysis and the network cluster tests, from the derived spectrograms deposited in dandiset 001347.
